### `pol_eco_board_notifications`

Stores every notification event generated for users, including delivery
status, event type, recipient linkage, and time stamps. Each record
represents a single notification instance requiring delivery and history
retention independent from participation or content actions. Links to the
intended user (member, moderator, or admin) via foreign key, and
optionally to the related provider and originating post/comment/report as
appropriate. Enables audit trail for notifications and supports
operational, compliance, and privacy purge requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `recipient_member_id`
  > Recipient's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). References the user to whom
  > the notification is delivered (can be member, moderator, or admin).
- `provider_id`
  > Notification provider's [pol_eco_board_notification_providers.id](#pol_eco_board_notification_providers).
  > Identifies the provider/service used for this notification attempt.
- `event_type`
  > Business event type code or category, e.g., 'reply', 'moderation_action',
  > 'report_status', 'admin_notice'. Used for filtering and analytics.
- `related_object_id`
  > UUID of related business object (e.g., post, comment, report, etc.) for
  > audit and navigation. References the source event but is not a foreign
  > key to keep polymorphism. Can be null for global or system-wide
  > notifications.
- `status`
  > Current delivery status of the notification (e.g., 'pending',
  > 'delivered', 'failed'). Used for tracking and reporting.
- `attempt_count`
  > Number of delivery attempts made so far for this notification event. Used
  > for retry/backoff logic and audit.
- `last_attempted_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent delivery attempt for this notification.
  > Updated on each send try, used for troubleshooting and audit.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when notification was successfully delivered. Set if and only
  > if status is 'delivered'. Null otherwise.
- `created_at`
  > Created timestamp for audit trail; when the notification was initially
  > generated.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp; reflects status/attempt count updates.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for privacy purge. Null if notification is active.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_preferences`

Holds explicit notification opt-in/out settings and channel preferences
for each member, separated from user profile for privacy and audit
clarity. Each row applies to a single user and event type/channel
combination, supporting granular user control and compliance evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > User's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). References the member whose
  > preference is being recorded.
- `event_type`
  > Type of event this preference relates to (e.g., 'reply',
  > 'moderation_action', 'admin_notice').
- `channel`
  > Delivery channel: 'email', 'push', 'in_app', or 'sms' (enumerate in
  > application logic, not DB constraint at this level).
- `opt_in`
  > Whether the member has explicitly opted in (true) or out (false) of this
  > notification type/channel combination. Used for privacy and regulatory
  > compliance.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp preference was first recorded. Supports opt-in/out consent
  > auditability.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last preference change or user update.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_failures`

Retains all failed notification delivery attempts, supporting technical
diagnostics, reporting, and compliance audits. Each row records a failure
for a specific notification, including provider, technical details, and
timestamps. Enables operational and privacy retention policies for
notification-specific failures.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `notification_id`
  > Associated notification's [pol_eco_board_notifications.id](#pol_eco_board_notifications). Each
  > failure is tied to an attempted notification event.
- `provider_id`
  > Provider involved in the failed delivery (references {@link
  > pol_eco_board_notification_providers.id}). May be null where failure is
  > internal to system and not a provider.
- `failure_code`
  > Provider- or system-assigned error code describing the reason for failure
  > (business-level string, not system enum).
- `failure_message`
  > Human-readable summary of the failure cause, suitable for diagnostics,
  > audit, and support.
- `occurred_at`
  > Timestamp when the failure was recorded or detected. Used for analytics
  > and time-slicing incident review.
- `resolution_status`
  > Resolution or status of the failure event: e.g., 'pending', 'resolved',
  > 'permanent_failure'. For operational reporting and closure.
- `created_at`
  > Created timestamp for record/audit. Indicates when the failure was
  > entered.
- `updated_at`: Updated timestamp to track changes in resolution/status.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for compliance or privacy purge, may be null if
  > not yet deleted.

### `pol_eco_board_external_auth_providers`

Represents authorized external authentication providers (e.g., Google,
Facebook, Apple) integrated for polEcoBoard user sign-in flows. Used for
compliance, audit, and dynamic provider switching. Each record uniquely
identifies a provider, manages status (enabled/disabled), and stores
privacy/compliance settings relevant to integration. Does not contain
user authentication data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_name`
  > The human-readable name of the authentication provider (e.g., Google,
  > Facebook, Apple).
- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal key or code identifying the provider integration (e.g.,
  > 'google', 'facebook'). Used for configuration and provider switching.
- `status`
  > Current status of the provider integration. Valid values: 'enabled',
  > 'disabled', 'maintenance'. Enforces which providers are available to the
  > system.
- `privacy_policy_uri`: The URI to the provider's privacy policy for compliance display to users.
- `data_residency_region`
  > Region/jurisdiction where user data processed by this provider is stored
  > or resides (ISO region/country code, e.g., 'US', 'EU').
- `consent_required`
  > Specifies whether explicit user consent is required for this provider
  > integration per privacy/compliance rules.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of provider record creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last record update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion, or null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_third_party_audit_logs`

Tracks all events, actions, and error responses from external
integrations (e.g., authentication, analytics, anti-spam, notification
providers) for compliance/audit purposes. Each log entry records source
provider, event type, event payload (as JSON/string), timestamp, system
result code, and related correlation information, supporting
troubleshooting, legal hold, and system incident management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > Internal code identifying which external provider generated the event
  > (e.g., 'google', 'analytics', 'anti_spam').
- `event_type`
  > Type or category of event logged (e.g., 'auth_flow_start',
  > 'auth_flow_error', 'api_call', 'token_refresh', 'notification_send',
  > 'fallback').
- `event_payload`
  > Serialized JSON string or encoded payload of the event as received from
  > or sent to the external provider.
- `result_code`
  > Internal result code or error indicator derived from processing the
  > provider event (e.g., 'success', 'failure', 'timeout', 'invalid_token').
- `correlation_id`
  > Optional provider, system, or business correlation/trace ID for boundary
  > tracking across systems (e.g., trace IDs for business audit).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

### `pol_eco_board_analytics_events`

Stores anonymized, structured events transmitted to analytics platforms
(e.g., page view, post creation, vote action, login) for
operational/business intelligence and compliance. Each record supports
audit requirements, regional reporting, and opt-in/out model. Not linked
to user identities to preserve privacy. Data is purged or aggregated as
per retention rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `event_type`
  > Business-defined type of analytics event (e.g., 'page_view', 'login',
  > 'vote', 'moderation_action').
- `session_anon_id`
  > Anonymized session identifier (non-PII, no user linkage), used for
  > statistical correlation of analytics events by session or cohort.
- `user_role`
  > User role associated with the event (e.g., 'guest', 'member',
  > 'moderator', 'admin'). Used for business segmentation.
- `event_details`
  > JSON-encoded details or metadata specific to the analytics event (e.g.,
  > category, target_id, feature usage); varies by event_type.
- `region`
  > Region or jurisdiction associated with the event/session (data residency,
  > reporting compliance; ISO country/region code).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the analytics event was generated.

### `pol_eco_board_anti_spam_events`

Captures event records for all interactions with anti-spam/abuse
prevention integrations (inbound or outbound events). Stores provider,
operation, content hash, action outcome, score, and related metadata for
audit and investigation, supporting appeals, escalations, and incident
reviews. Does not store original user content (use hash/fingerprint
only).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal code or key for the integrated anti-spam provider (e.g.,
  > 'akismet', 'custom_1').
- `operation`
  > Business or technical operation performed (e.g., 'content_submit',
  > 'abuse_check', 'appeal', 'score_retrieval').
- `content_hash`
  > Hash or digital fingerprint of content analyzed (never stores raw user
  > content; only hashed to protect privacy).
- `score`
  > Numeric risk or abuse probability score output from the provider (e.g.,
  > 0.00 to 1.00; higher is more risky).
- `action_taken`
  > Result of anti-spam event or system action (e.g., 'approved', 'blocked',
  > 'escalated', 'queued', 'error').
- `appeal_requested`
  > Indicates if appeal process (user- or moderator-initiated) was requested
  > for this event.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when anti-spam event was recorded.

### `pol_eco_board_consent_statuses`

Stores all explicit consent and opt-in/out statuses by provider, data
region, and integration use, supporting regulatory compliance for user
and session privacy. Tracks what was consented to, for which provider, by
which region/session/date, and manages enforcement of business/legal data
flows. No PII is stored (refer to session/user separately in other
domains for linkage).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > The unique key or code for the provider or integration to which consent
  > applies (e.g., 'analytics', 'auth', 'notification').
- `region`
  > Jurisdiction or regional code relevant to the consent (for data residency
  > and privacy enforcement, ISO format).
- `consent_type`
  > Type of consent (e.g., 'analytics', 'email_marketing', 'third_party',
  > 'profiling').
- `consent_status`
  > Status of the consent. Valid values: 'opt_in', 'opt_out', 'revoked',
  > 'pending'.
- `session_anon_id`
  > Anonymized session or cohort identifier related to this consent record
  > (no PII/user identity stored).
- `audit_trail`
  > JSON-encoded object/log with consent action metadata (e.g., time, source,
  > device, evidence), for compliance audit. No PII included.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the consent status was recorded.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_providers`

Catalogs all external notification providers (e.g., SendGrid, Twilio
Email, SMTP, SMS) integrated with the service. Each record defines
supported channels, endpoint URIs, operational status, provider region,
configuration metadata (non-secret), and business flags for
routing/fallback logic. Used for compliance transparency and operational
provider switching.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_name`
  > Human-readable name of the notification provider (e.g., 'SendGrid',

- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal key/code representing notification integration (e.g.,
  > 'sendgrid', 'twilio_sms').
- `channels_supported`
  > Comma-separated string of notification channels supported by this
  > provider (e.g., 'email,sms,push').
- `endpoint_uri`
  > Integration endpoint URI for provider's main API/service (primary
  > endpoint, not credential/secret).
- `region`
  > Provider's service or business region, for data residency and routing

- `status`
  > Current operational status of the provider: 'active', 'inactive', or
  > 'maintenance'.
- `config_metadata`
  > JSON-encoded key/value mapping of non-secret configuration and
  > operational metadata (supported features, documentation links, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of provider record creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last provider config update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion, or null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_operational_logs`

Centralized log of all system operations, events, and service activities
for the polEcoBoard platform. Captures timestamped records of API calls,
backend jobs, system notifications, performance events, and other
significant operational actions for audit and monitoring. Provides a
historical record to support incident investigation, compliance
verification, and operational analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `log_level`
  > Severity or categorization of the operational event (e.g., INFO, WARNING,
  > ERROR, CRITICAL). Used for triaging and dashboard filtering.
- `logged_at`: Timestamp when the operational log entry was recorded.
- `message`
  > Human-readable description or summary of the operational event. Designed
  > for audit readability and system monitoring dashboards.
- `context`
  > Structured or serialized metadata providing extra context for the
  > operational event (e.g., job type, subsystem, trace ID, related resource
  > identifiers).
- `actor_id`
  > Optional reference to the involved admin, moderator, or automated system
  > actor. May be null if operation is system-initiated or anonymous.
- `event_code`
  > Internal code or short identifier for the event type, supporting analytic
  > and automation use-cases (e.g. 'SIGN_IN', 'BACKUP_START',
  > 'MAINTENANCE_NOTICE').
- `created_at`
  > Log record creation timestamp (for soft-deletion and audit lifecycle
  > control).
- `updated_at`: Log record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if log is active.

### `pol_eco_board_audit_trails`

Immutable, write-once audit trail storing high-sensitivity business and
system change records required for compliance reviews, security
monitoring, and regulatory audits. Includes detailed context for all
critical actions (e.g., config changes, access grants/revocations, data
retention actions, incident resolutions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `action_type`
  > Type of audited action (e.g., CONFIG_CHANGE, ROLE_ASSIGN, DATA_ERASURE,

- `performed_by_id`: ID of admin or privileged actor responsible for the action.
- `target_resource`
  > Unique or composite identifier of the resource subject to the action
  > (could be user id, config id, or resource URI).
- `audit_context`
  > Structured or serialized details about action, pre/post state, or
  > business justification.
- `recorded_at`: Timestamp when the audit trail entry was written (immutable once set).
- `created_at`
  > Audit entry creation timestamp (redundant for retention lifecycle and
  > index support).
- `updated_at`
  > Audit entry last update timestamp (in principle, should not change except
  > for retention lifecycle metadata changes).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp; null means audit entry is live and protected

Service incident management and business-impact event log for

reports, including outages, degraded services, compliance issues, data

business review, and regulatory reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `incident_code`
  > Unique, short string code for the business or operational incident (e.g.,
  > OUTAGE_2024_05, GDPR_BREACH_001).
- `category`
  > Classification of the incident (e.g., OUTAGE, BREACH, COMPLIANCE, LEGAL,
  > MAINTENANCE). Used for admin filtering and regulatory response.
- `status`
  > Current business status of the incident (e.g., OPEN, RESOLVED, ESCALATED,
  > UNDER_REVIEW, CLOSED).
- `description`: Summary of what happened, business impact, and affected services/users.
- `detected_at`
  > Timestamp when the incident was first detected (may be earlier than
  > creation for retroactive records).
- `resolved_at`
  > When the incident was resolved or marked as closed; null for
  > ongoing/outstanding incidents.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit and operational lifecycle management.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if still primary record.

### `pol_eco_board_maintenance_windows`

Scheduled and historical system maintenance windows, covering downtimes,
upgrades, migrations, and other planned/unplanned service interruptions.
Supports platform status dashboards, incident correlation, and regulatory
notifications. Used for compliance tracking and SLA verification.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `window_code`
  > Unique identifier for the maintenance window event (e.g., MAINT_2025Q1,
  > HOTFIX_20240615).
- `start_time`: Scheduled or actual maintenance window start timestamp.
- `end_time`
  > Scheduled or actual maintenance window end timestamp; null if still
  > ongoing or if unplanned duration.
- `expected_impact`
  > Human-readable summary of expected service impact; for admin and
  > compliance dashboarding.
- `actual_impact`: Recorded impact as determined post-event.
- `notified_at`
  > Time when admins/moderators were notified of the scheduled/unscheduled
  > maintenance event.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if still in operational window history.

### `pol_eco_board_service_metrics`

Aggregated, time-bucketed service-level metrics supporting operational
dashboards, business KPI tracking, and SLA verification for polEcoBoard.
Metrics include post/comment/vote counts, user activity, moderation
actions, response times, operational error frequencies, and
retention/purge statistics. Only computed via backend aggregation; no
denormalized materialized view pattern needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `metric_code`
  > Short string code identifying metric type (e.g., POST_COUNT,
  > COMMENT_COUNT, VOTE_VOLUME, API_LATENCY, INCIDENT_COUNT, PURGE_VOLUME).
- `metric_window_start`: Start of the aggregation time window (e.g., hour, day, week).
- `metric_window_end`: End of the aggregation window (exclusive).
- `value_int`
  > Integer-valued metric (e.g., count of events, users, incidents in the
  > window).
- `value_double`
  > Floating-point metric (e.g., average latency, percent completion, ratio).
  > Only one of value_int or value_double typically used per metric by code
  > convention.
- `notes`
  > Optional business note or free-form annotation to explain anomalies or
  > correlate business events with metric deviations.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for when the metric aggregation entry was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Last time metric was updated (e.g., for amended calculations or corrected
  > data).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, for retention/purge control. Null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_business_reports`

Business event report entry for admin dashboards, export/audit actions,
scheduled metrics, regulatory filings, or compliance reviews. Covers both
automatically and manually triggered reports, their configuration,
delivery status, and role in audit trail. Enables tracking, lifecycle
management, and historical analysis of all formal business report
objects.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_code`
  > Short string code or business key identifying the report (e.g.,
  > WEEKLY_METRICS_20240810, INCIDENT_EXPORT_20250515).
- `report_type`
  > Business categorization of the report (e.g., METRICS, AUDIT, INCIDENTS,
  > EXPORT, SLA, LEGAL, COMPLIANCE).
- `status`
  > Report status in the report lifecycle (e.g., PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED,
  > DELIVERED).
- `requested_by_id`
  > Admin or system service account that initiated the business report
  > request or generation.
- `content_uri`
  > Location or reference (e.g., S3 URI) of the generated report document or
  > export file.
- `triggered_at`: Timestamp when the report generation/export was started.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when report was delivered or made available for download; null
  > for pending reports.
- `failure_reason`
  > If the report failed to complete or deliver, this provides the reason or
  > error context.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp on report object creation (for lifecycle and retention
  > tracking).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (for report lifecycle changes).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if report record is active.
